review_notes: I read the whole file, which has one theorem. I also read the general lemma it uses, `high_full_prime_envelope_tail_uniform` in PrimeTailHighProduct.lean, and the angular copy of the same proof. The file's theorem is deliberately the specialisation of that general lemma to the prime-group index types, R = 2 and the fixed `primeProductEnvelope`. The general lemma already handles arbitrary index types, arbitrary R ≥ 1 and arbitrary smooth compactly supported envelopes. All hypotheses (the A/B range conditions, the T lower bound, H ≤ B^3) are copied unchanged from that lemma, and I found no weaker condition that the proof supports. I did not find a useful generalisation that would not require new mathematics. The stated R = 2 and `primeProductEnvelope` are the concrete application the file exists to provide, so I do not count them as a defect. I could not run Lean, so I did not test any alternative form.
